title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Now Runs at 60 FPS on PC Emulators Lichii and Eglantine, a Day After Booting at 20-30 FPS - Wccftech
summary: The Nintendo Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time already runs at 60 frames per second on various PC emulators.
text:
Yesterday we reported that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake was booting on PC at 15 to 30 FPS within hours of its official Switch 2 launch, albeit with heavy visual glitches. Just a day later, the situation has already massively improved.

DSOGaming reports that the Lichii emulator has fixed most of the remake’s visual issues in a single day, with the starting area and the Great Deku Tree now running at 60 FPS rather than the 20-30 FPS of launch day. One user on X went further, describing the latest build as running at a stable 4K 60 FPS with clear visuals , no bloom problem, no artifacts, and no slow motion, with only minor stutters and freezing left.

Separately, a Discord user running a 5700X CPU and RTX 5070 GPU with precompiled shaders reported in the Eglantine server reaching the Kokiri Sword from a new save with texture flickering still present on foliage and ground, a lighting fault on the Great Deku Tree during the opening animation, desynced audio in parts of the first cinematic, and slowdowns from low framerate. Which is roughly where you'd expect a two-day-old compatibility effort to be . Still, their video demonstrates a largely playable game, as you can see in the embed below.

The Eglantine repository shows the frantic activity of the modding team to improve Ocarina of Time compatibility. Lichii is a fork of Eglantine, which itself builds on Eden, yuzu and Sudachi, and Eglantine has pushed two Ocarina-specific test branches in the past day alone .

text:

Apple’s iPhone Duo has been officially on sale for two weeks, and the company said today that the App Store now has over 100,000 apps that are built for the foldable.

“It’s been wonderful to see how quickly developers have embraced iPhone Duo, and we’re grateful for their creativity and innovation,” Susan Prescott, Apple’s VP of Worldwide Developer Relations, says in a statement. “Today there are well over 100,000 apps built for iPhone Duo already live on the App Store, and thousands of optimized apps are being added to the store each day.” Prescott adds that “the enthusiasm has been incredible, and we’re excited to see the pace of updates continue to accelerate as more and more apps optimize for iPhone Duo.”

Although there are now many apps that are optimized for the Duo, they can sometimes still have some issues. title: Apple Rumored to Drop the iPhone's Action Button Next Year - MacRumors
summary: Apple plans to merge the iPhone's Action button with the Camera Control starting next year, according to the leaker known as "Instant Digital". In a new post on Weibo, the leaker claimed that a single press of the combined button would open the camera, while a long press would trigger the function assigned to the Action button. They explicitly clarified that the dedicated Action button would disappear, while the Camera Control button would remain.
text:
Apple plans to merge the iPhone's Action button with the Camera Control starting next year, according to the leaker known as " Instant Digital ."

In a new post on Weibo, the leaker claimed that a single press of the combined button would open the camera, while a long press would trigger the function assigned to the Action button. They explicitly clarified that the dedicated Action button would disappear, while the Camera Control button would remain.

The proposed arrangement seems plausible given how the two features already work. The Action button predates the Camera Control and requires a long press to activate its assigned function, while a single press of the Camera Control opens the camera. Combining them in the way described would therefore preserve both familiar interactions, with the customizable action simply moving to a different location on the device.

A long press of Camera Control currently opens Visual Intelligence , but that feature has since been integrated directly into the Camera app as Siri mode in iOS 27 . That integration could give Apple room to reassign the gesture while keeping Visual Intelligence accessible through the Camera app.

It is notable that the iPhone Duo also lacks an Action button , despite retaining Camera Control. Its omission provides a precedent for an iPhone without the separate control and could hint at a broader change in the future.

But the moments when I do take advantage of directly manipulating software with my fingers are beneficial enough that it’s suddenly disappointing to switch back to regular Macs. Apple chose to ease users into this new way of interacting with the MacBook Pro instead of radically overhauling macOS to be more finger-friendly. Touch is an option that’s there when you want it, but it’s never a nuisance.

title: The Headphones That Came With the First Sony Walkman Are Back, Now With USB-C - Hypebeast
text:
Wired headphones Sony revives the original Walkman headphones, adds USB-C Orange ear cushions included.

106 ... ... ... A woman wearing Sony's new MDR-3R USB-C headphones. Credit: Sony A woman wearing Sony's new MDR-3R USB-C headphones. Credit: Sony Text settings Story text Size Small Standard Large Width * Standard Wide Links Standard Orange * Subscribers only Learn more Minimize to nav Color us nostalgic.

Sony has brought back the MDR-3-series headphones that debuted in 1979 alongside the Walkman TPS-L2 cassette player.

Originally called the “MDR-3L2,” the first Walkman headphones were known for their sleek, adjustable gray plastic headband, which extended via metal sliders and ended in signature orange, circular ear cushions. The lightweight, on-ear headphones are a contrast to the bulky headsets that are popular these days, which use wide, cushioned headbands for long-term comfort and large earcups that can support big drivers and are often heavily padded for noise isolation.

The new MDR-3R (note the slightly different name) headphones look just like the originals and come with orange and blue ear cushions.

New headphones are often wireless these days, but the MDR-3R continues the wired tradition of the MDR-3, with an essential twist: a USB-C connector.

“The MDR-3R has been redesigned for modern use while preserving the experience value of freely taking music out into the world, which the original MDR-3 helped popularize,” Sony’s announcement says.

title: YouTube is giving its Android navigation bar a Liquid Glass-y makeover - Android Authority
summary: YouTube unveiled a new navigation bar design that noticeably omits the "Subscriptions" option, instead relabels it as "Subs" and it's only at the top menu.
text:
Chayjitti Hongmanee/Shutterstock Add BGR on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover YouTube is no stranger to making arbitrary changes users just cannot stand. While some cool new features added to the video-sharing platform more recently optimized the user experience with features like conversational search and On-the-go mode, others, like when YouTube made users' TV experience worse on purpose via unskippable ads, show the company isn't completely tuned in to what people enjoy and loathe about its interface.

It seems the latest alteration to the app's navigation bar warrants several thumbs down – that is, if users can find the dislike button . In November 2026, YouTube unveiled a new navigation bar design that noticeably omits the "Subscriptions" option. The button, labeled "Subs," unassumingly hides on the top menu between the Home and Movies & TV options. Needless to say, some users were annoyed to discover the tab was no longer in its usual location.

"Who on earth decided that this is good design?" one Reddit user asked. The "Library" tab is also noticeably missing in action. Users now must navigate to their profiles to be able to view recent videos, downloads, playlists, and other selections usually found in their libraries. On top of moving these buttons to another location, users also observed that YouTube gave the navigation bar a liquid glass finish and a floating presentation.
